# reac-repacer / fuzz_wire

reac-repacer's own fuzz target `fuzz_wire` ([source](source/fuzz_wire.c), unmodified), which OSS-Fuzz does not run, over reac-repacer 0.2.3 (FreeREAC/reac-repacer at 3ac1cf10).

Takes one flag byte (the broadcast-only switch and a channel slot from -2 to 125) and then a frame, cut to the 1600 bytes of the daemon's receive buffer. It runs the frame through every reader the daemon applies to a frame from the wire: the forward classifier, the return relay, the downstream listener, the clock meter, the counter read, the channel-width rule, the tag-removing copy reader and the slot sample reader. It compares each answer with one the harness computes itself from the REAC frame layout.

## How this program differs from a libFuzzer build of this fuzz target
- Linked against a static library of src/repace_wire.c and src/repace_conf.c, and one of libreac's src/reac.c, the files reac-repacer's own libFuzzer build compiles; built as a static riscv64 program for the standard driver in place of libFuzzer.
- In every build, getenv() returns NULL, getpid() returns 1 and mkstemp() uses a fixed name, so the program depends only on its input.
- A small driver reads the input file, calls the fuzz target one to four times and prints each return value.

## What the harness checks
- The forward reader queues a REAC frame of 18 bytes or more (with broadcast-only, only one whose destination starts with 0xff) as audio when its type is 00 00 and as control otherwise, and drops every other frame ([lines 50-70](source/fuzz_wire.c#L50-L70)): abort(); not confirmed in the binary.
- The return relay passes exactly the REAC frames of 14 bytes or more ([lines 72-84](source/fuzz_wire.c#L72-L84)): abort(); not confirmed in the binary.
- The downstream listener accepts exactly the REAC frames of 18 bytes or more, untagged or behind one 802.1Q VLAN tag ([lines 86-98](source/fuzz_wire.c#L86-L98)): abort(); not confirmed in the binary.
- The clock meter counts exactly the REAC frames of 1000 bytes or more, untagged or tagged, reads the frame counter as the two little-endian bytes after the EtherType, and leaves the counter unchanged for a frame it skips ([lines 100-131](source/fuzz_wire.c#L100-L131)): abort(); not confirmed in the binary.
- For a frame of 18 bytes or more, the counter read is bytes 14-15, little-endian ([lines 133-144](source/fuzz_wire.c#L133-L144)): abort(); not confirmed in the binary.
- The channel width of a frame length is the frame law's (52 bytes plus 36 per channel, for an even width from 2 to 40, or 2 bytes more with an FCS residue), and no negative length has a width ([lines 146-168](source/fuzz_wire.c#L146-L168)): abort(); not confirmed in the binary.
- The copy reader keeps exactly the REAC audio frames of 50 bytes or more; a tagged one loses its four tag bytes and nothing else moves ([lines 184-210](source/fuzz_wire.c#L184-L210)): abort(); not confirmed in the binary.
- A slot is read only when the frame is audio and its width holds the slot; the 12 samples read are the ones the REAC braid layout places there, sign-extended from 24 bits; a declined read leaves the samples unchanged ([lines 212-251](source/fuzz_wire.c#L212-L251)): abort(); not confirmed in the binary.

## Builds
Static riscv64 Linux programs, compiled for RV64G and run as `<file> <input-file>`; `oft fetch reac-repacer` downloads the published ones and checks each against its SHA-256.

Each build also links code that no sanitizer instruments, as its link recorded it. A statement about a sanitizer build covers that code only as uninstrumented code: ASan checks no load or store made inside it, and UBSan inserts no check there.

- plain: `clang_rt.crtbegin.o` (compiler-rt), `libclang_rt.builtins.a` (compiler-rt), `crt1.o` (the C library), `libc.a` (the C library)
- ubsan: `clang_rt.crtbegin.o` (compiler-rt), `libclang_rt.builtins.a` (compiler-rt), `crt1.o` (the C library), `libc.a` (the C library)
- asan: `clang_rt.crtbegin.o` (compiler-rt), `libclang_rt.asan.a` (the sanitizer runtime), `libclang_rt.builtins.a` (compiler-rt), `crt1.o` (the C library), `libc.a` (the C library), `libunwind.a` (the C++ runtime)
